fields.domain_description: Products are the things an organisation buys, makes or sells, at every level of processing and packing — ingredients, packaging components, part-made goods, finished packs and cases — together with what each is defined to be and what it is made from. Includes the batches in which they are made or received. Excludes the individual serial-numbered units made to a product definition, which are Instances, and the financial instruments an organisation issues or trades, which are Instruments.

Instances are individually identified physical things — a serial-numbered pack, a machine, a vessel, a tool — each made to a product definition and traceable as itself for its whole life. Includes what is fitted into each and what condition it is in. Excludes the product definition it is made to, which is a Product, and the batch it belongs to where it is not individually identified, which is a concept of Products.

Equipment covers the places in a plant where work is performed — site, area, work centre, work unit and equipment module — what each is able to do, and the rules that constrain what may run there. Includes the plant structure as ISA-95 defines it. Excludes the machines that stand in those places, which are Instances, and the geographic places goods are held at, which are Locations.

Processes are the defined steps of work by which products are made — mixing, pasteurising, filling, labelling — the order they run in, the settings they run at, and the recipes that state them at each level of specificity from formulation to the instructions issued for one batch. Includes what each step requires of equipment, people and materials. Excludes what a product is made from, which is Products, and the record of a step actually being performed, which is an Event.

Locations are identifiable geographic places at which things are held or handled — a site, a plant, a warehouse, a storage position within one — the conditions each must keep, and the identifiers each is known by. Includes places operated by other organisations where goods are received from or delivered to. Excludes the production structure within a site, which is Equipment.

The kind of hazard a product carries, and therefore which declaration regime applies to it.
The scheme an identifier belongs to.
How specific a recipe is, following ISA-88.
The level of a place in the plant structure, following ISA-95.
Why production stopped, from a governed list.
What is done with material that failed its specification.
What kind of exchange a transaction is.
The unit a quantity is expressed in. Used wherever a quantity is recorded.

fields.concept_description: One qualification a person holds to perform particular work, with the basis on which it was awarded.
One period a person was assigned to work at a place.
One signature a person applied to a record — what was signed, when, and what the signature meant.
One assessment of a supplier or outside manufacturer — its scope, its result, and how long it is valid.
One problem formally raised with a supplier, with their response and its closure.
One property a document states about a batch or product, and whether the organisation verified it.
One thing the organisation buys, makes or sells, at one level of processing or packing.
One identifier by which a product is known, in one scheme.
One version of what a product must be, with its limits and how conformance is checked.
One complete statement of what goes into a product, for a site, market or period.
One quantity made or received as one unit of traceability, with its lot code and date.
One part of a batch separated for handling, retaining its link to the batch.
One hazard a product carries — an allergen, an irritant, a classified chemical — with the basis of the declaration.
One ingredient a product must disclose, how much of it there is, and whether it is withheld as confidential.
One stated country or region of origin, with the basis of the statement.
How long a product lasts under one set of storage conditions.
One approved alternative for an input, with the conditions for using it.
One way the members of a family differ — size, format, pack count — and the values allowed.
The expected or actual cost of a product, by element, for a period.
One change to a product, and whether it made a new product or a new version of what goes in.
One individually identified physical thing — a serialised pack or a machine — made to a product definition.
One identifier by which a unit is individually known, in one scheme.
One reading of a unit's state — hours run, cycles, wear, calibration result.
One way a machine characteristically fails, and what that failure causes.
One assessment of how much a machine matters — to output, to safety, and whether a spare exists.
One place in a plant where work is performed — a site level, an area, a work centre, a work unit, an equipment module.
One identifier by which a place is known, in one scheme.
One thing a place is able to do, and how much of it.
One constraint on what may run after what at a place, with the reason.
One planned maintenance regime for a place, and what triggers it.
One step of work, defined independently of any product — mixing, pasteurising, filling.
One thing a step needs to run — a capability, a qualification, a kind of material.
One setting a step can be run at, with the range allowed.
One rule stating what is sampled at a step, when, how much, and against which specification.
The steps, in order, that turn a product's inputs into the product.
One statement of a routing at one level of specificity — general, site, master, or the instructions for one batch.
One value set for a setting at one recipe level, for one product at one place.
One identifiable place — a site, a plant, a warehouse, a storage position.
One identifier by which a place is known, and who issued it.
One condition a place must keep — temperature, humidity — with its limits.
One exchange of goods of a stated kind — a purchase, a receipt, an issue to production, a transfer, a despatch.
One line of an exchange: one product, one quantity, one batch.
One quantity of a product, in one condition, at one place, at one time.
One thing that happened in the operation, at a time and a place.
One instruction to make a quantity of a product.
One batch actually made — what was instructed, what was done, and what came out.
One quantity of one input batch used in one run, filling one place in the recipe.
One batch divided into parts, or several combined into one.
One change of a place from one product to another, including any clean.
One stop in production at one place — start, end, and why.
One piece of maintenance work — what prompted it, what was found, what was done.
One test against a specification — its method, its sample and its result.
One departure from a defined procedure during a run.
One failure of a batch or material against its specification.
One decision about failed material, with its reason and its approver.
One response to a problem — its cause, what was done, the check that it worked, and its closure.
One act of making output available, by one person, on a stated basis.
One safety or quality incident, its scope and its resolution.
One report from outside the organisation about a product.
One correction to something already recorded, replacing it without erasing it.
One period a place failed to keep its required conditions.
